public_rationale: Marcus said that outside coders and tech fans, much of the world feels differently about ChatGPT at work. Two 2024 surveys back this up. In Upwork's April-May 2024 survey, 77% of employees who use AI said the tools added to their workload, and 47% said they did not know how to get the expected gains. In Pew's October 2024 survey of US workers, most did not use chatbots at work. Of non-users, 36% said a major reason was that the tools have no use in their job. Among users, only 40% rated chatbots very helpful for speed and 29% for quality. Together these show that a large share of ordinary workers were lukewarm, negative, or indifferent. Pew also found that many regular users did find the tools highly helpful, so positive views were not limited to coders. That tempers the claim but does not undo it.
limitations: 'Much of' has no threshold. The outcome depends on reading it as a large share, not a majority.
The surveys cover AI tools or chatbots in general, not ChatGPT alone, and do not split out tech workers.
Upwork's survey was commissioned by a company that sells freelance services, which its findings promote.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Outside coders and tech fans, many workers do not view ChatGPT favourably as a work tool.

statement.excerpt: Many coders and tech aficionados may love ChatGPT for work, but much of the outside world feels quite differently.
statement.document_title: Most people don’t think GenAI has improved their productivity

from_speaker: Many coders and tech aficionados may love ChatGPT for work
much of the outside world feels quite differently
said in the context of the Upwork survey of workers, July 2024
our_interpretation: Plain reading: in 2024, a substantial share of ordinary workers (not just a fringe) did not see ChatGPT or similar generative AI tools as clearly useful for their work. Signs of this include saying the tools added to their workload, not finding them very helpful, or seeing no use for them in their job.
'Much of' is read as a large minority or more, not necessarily a majority.
Marcus named no period. Because he describes a state at the time of the post, the target period is calendar 2024, the year of the post, which covers surveys taken shortly before and after it.
Surveys of the general workforce are accepted as evidence for 'the outside world'. Coders and tech fans are a small share of those samples, but the surveys do not remove them.
criteria.support_condition: Credible 2024 worker surveys show that a substantial share of workers in general, or of non-tech workers, report that generative AI or chatbots added to their workload, were not very helpful, or had no use in their job.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible 2024 worker surveys show broad, majority enthusiasm for ChatGPT or generative AI as a work tool among ordinary workers, with only small shares negative or indifferent.

evidence.excerpt: 77% of employees using AI say these tools have added to their workload, and nearly half (47%) of employees using AI report they do not know how to achieve the expected productivity gains.
evidence.explanation: In a survey of full-time employees in four countries (April-May 2024), most employees who use AI said it added to their workload. That is a negative work experience shared by many ordinary workers.

evidence.excerpt: Among workers who have used AI chatbots for work, 40% say these tools have been extremely or very helpful in allowing them to do things more quickly. A smaller share (29%) say they have been highly helpful in improving the quality of their work.
evidence.locator: section 'Do workers find AI chatbots helpful for their work?', paragraph 1
evidence.explanation: In October 2024, most US workers who had used chatbots such as ChatGPT did not rate them as highly helpful for speed (60%) or quality (71%). That is far from universal enthusiasm.

evidence.excerpt: Among workers who are not AI chatbot users, 36% say a major reason they have never used AI chatbots for work is that there isn’t any use for them in their job.
evidence.locator: section 'Why some workers have not used AI chatbots for work', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: Pew found that 69% of workers did not use chatbots at work. Of those non-users, over a third said a major reason is that the tools have no use in their job. This shows widespread indifference outside the enthusiast groups.

evidence.excerpt: Among workers who use AI chatbots regularly, 54% say they’ve been highly helpful in speeding up their work and 41% say they’ve been highly helpful in improving their work quality.
evidence.locator: section 'Do workers find AI chatbots helpful for their work?', paragraph 5
evidence.explanation: Counterevidence: a meaningful share of workers, especially regular users, found chatbots highly helpful. So positive views were not confined to coders. This tempers the claim but does not refute 'much of the outside world feels differently'.
